answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock capital for every fake identity, tying up funds and risking losses; creating more accounts no longer comes free. The mesa market can route claims through willow reviewers, while a reef of shared audit records makes repeated abuse easier to detect. This raises the cost of attack without assuming identities are unique.
